name: Platform admin dashboard and business operations

epics.name: Admin platform: staff roles, TOTP MFA, sessions, re-auth
epics.goal: Least-privilege staff access with mandatory TOTP, short sessions, re-auth for high-risk actions and the auth gaps closed, so support/finance/ops can be onboarded safely.

epics.name: Users and the support toolkit
epics.goal: One user page answers every support ticket: entitlements explained, account fixes, debug panel, timeline, consented read-only view-as, privacy summary.

epics.name: Customers, billing operations and retention
epics.goal: See who pays, whose card failed, comp a plan, issue promo codes, record refund notes, mirror cancellation reasons, sync the CRM, reconcile Stripe.

epics.name: Catalog, entitlements and the margin guard
epics.goal: Prices, limits and feature keys live in the database and are edited from admin behind a margin guard (80 % subscriptions / 20 % services).

epics.name: AI cost governance
epics.goal: Platform and per-user budgets as hard stops, per-feature cost, rule-based anomaly alerts, kill switches and abuse controls so AI spend can never run away.

epics.name: Runtime settings, feature flags, announcements, extension remote config
epics.goal: Every feature's on/off switch, price, limit, cap, quota and default is set from the app admin settings page (typed settings registry + feature registry + flags + catalog + extension remote config) — never hard-coded; code ships safe defaults, admin decides (user decision 2026-10-11). Nothing needs a deploy or a store review to pause a feature, change a number or an ATS adapter.

epics.name: Job-source operations
epics.goal: Per-source sync, test, retry, pause and archive with a durable run ledger and real ingestion-health charts.

epics.name: Email and notification operations
epics.goal: A mail log, suppression list and Brevo webhooks make deliverability real; templates get editable copy; automations and notification etiquette are governed.

epics.name: Support queues: bug reports and inquiries
epics.goal: Priority, assignee, first-response SLA, grouping, export and user-linking on both queues; triage from a phone.

epics.name: Security and compliance operations
epics.goal: Security events, blocked IPs, abuse flags, the privacy-request queue, retention policies, legal versions with acceptance, and the subprocessor list.

epics.name: Observability, backups, restore drills, incidents
epics.goal: Backups actually run and are verified, every scheduled job has a ledger with run-now/pause, deployments and system events are recorded, incidents are declared from admin.

epics.name: Analytics and the event/metrics pipeline
epics.goal: A first-party product-event table and daily rollups replace every sample chart; what cannot be real is labelled decorative or removed.

epics.name: Audit log
epics.goal: Server-side filters, risk and area columns, audited CSV export, PII-view reasons, access reviews and a complete set of audited mutations.

epics.name: Experts and services marketplace admin
epics.goal: Vet experts, assign and track service orders, record payouts, watch quality.

epics.name: Organizations admin (platform side)
epics.goal: Tenants, seats, setup fees, invoices and billing disputes for organizations, built on the O* org model.

epics.name: Mobile admin, accessibility, QA and CI
epics.goal: A triage-first phone experience, 44 px targets, dark mode, keyboard paths, and the first automated web tests for admin.

epics.name: BI export and unit economics
epics.goal: Nightly anonymised exports to S3 and a unit-economics page (margin vs floor, cap-hit %, conversion, churn) with alert emails.
